children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares rose on Wednesday, led by a rebound in chipmakers on dip buying following five consecutive sessions of decline.
** The benchmark KOSPI
was up 44.63 points, or 0.74%, at 6,079.78 as of 0127 GMT, after rising more than 2% earlier in the session.
** On Tuesday, the index fell 5.5% to the lowest since July 30.

** "On Wall Street, AI semiconductor stocks turned higher, and major demand firms remained robust, triggering dip-buying sentiment despite anxiety around related sectors," said Seo Sang-young, an analyst at Mirae Asset Securities.
** "Recent drops in semiconductor stocks are somewhat excessive, if there is no big change to earnings outlook," Seo said.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
rose 1.72%, while peer SK Hynix
gained 1.04%. Earlier in the session, both chipmakers rose more than 3%.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
climbed 2.07%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were up 0.63% and up 1.20%, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
added 2.51%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
fell 1.66%.
** Of the total 912 traded issues, 534 shares advanced, while 327 declined.
** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 168.9 billion won ($126.05 million).
** The won was quoted at 1,340.9 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.04% higher than its previous close at 1,341.5.
** In money and debt markets, December futures on 3-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) lost 0.06 point to 102.92.
** The most liquid 3-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose by 2.9 basis points to 3.879%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
rose by 0.3 basis points to 4.255%.
